sections.content: You know the future of probability (*Estará en casa*) from B1 Unit 22 and the whole family of guessing words from B2 Unit 3, including *puede que* + subjunctive. Spanish also guesses with modal verbs, and each one shows a different degree of confidence. *Poder* is the least sure: *Puede estar enfermo* is "He may be ill". *Deber de* is a good guess from signs: *Debe de estar enfermo* is "He must be ill". *Tener que* is nearly certain, because you see no other explanation: *Tiene que ser él* is "It has to be him". For the past, add *haber* + a past participle: *Debe de haber salido*, *Puede haber salido*, *Tiene que haber salido*.
sections.title: How sure are you?
From less sure to more sure
rows: Tiene que ser él; nadie más tiene la llave.
It has to be him; nobody else has the key.

sections.content: *Tiene que ser él* is a guess because the verb is *ser* (or *estar*, or another verb that describes a state). *Tiene que salir* is a need. Watch also the difference between *Puede venir* (infinitive, "he may come") and *Puede que venga* (*que* + subjunctive, "it is possible that he comes"): the meaning is the same, but the grammar is not.
